NIS2 note: Entity-wide risk-analysis policy; the method is reusable, but the CRA needs product-level design risk treatment.
ISO 27001 note: ISMS risk method and secure development policy transfer; re-scope to product risks and Annex I items.
IEC 62443-4-1 clauses: SR-1; SR-2; SR-3; SD-1; SD-2; SD-4 (kit mapping; verify)
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Security context, threat model and secure design practices match risk-based design; JRC-ENISA lists 4-1. IACS-scoped.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Security-level selection gives a risk-graded catalogue; the risk assessment itself sits in IEC 62443-3-2.
EN 18031 note: Per-mechanism applicability decision trees, not a product risk assessment; EN 40000-1-4 replaces them with risk assessment.
EN 303 645 note: Fixed baseline, not risk-based; JRC-ENISA lists it for point (1) at a very high level.
NIST SSDF note: Security requirements, risk-based design and design review; usable process evidence but not EU-recognised.
CRA drafts* note: Purpose-built for point (1); passed formal vote but no OJ citation expected, so no presumption.

NIS2 note: Vulnerability handling in the entity's own acquisition and development; no release gate for products.
ISO 27001 note: Vulnerability management and testing cover operated systems; no product release gate for known exploitable vulnerabilities.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Vulnerability and penetration testing before release; JRC-ENISA: discovery covered, fixing before release not explicit.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No known-vulnerability requirement at release; see IEC 62443-4-1 SVV.
EN 18031 note: Up-to-date software without publicly known exploitable vulnerabilities; EN 40000-1-4 reuses GEC-1. RED scope.
EN 303 645 note: Vulnerability reporting and updates; JRC-ENISA: discovery covered, fixing before release not.
NIST SSDF clauses: PW.4; PW.7; PW.8; RV.1 (kit mapping; verify)
NIST SSDF note: Component reuse, code review, testing and vulnerability identification; no explicit no-known-exploitable release gate.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts; the vertical clause also passes vulnerabilities reported within 14 days or publicly mitigated.

NIS2 note: Does not address product-level secure-by-default configuration or reset.
ISO 27001 note: Configuration management of organisational systems; JRC-ENISA lists 27002 here, but no product defaults or reset.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Hardening guidelines document secure configuration; no requirement that the product ships secure by default or resets.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Configuration settings and least functionality; no explicit secure-default or factory-reset requirement.
EN 18031 note: Secure defaults only partly covered; Decision 2025/138 restricts presumption where users may skip passwords; no reset.
EN 303 645 note: No universal default passwords and minimised exposure; no general secure-default or reset requirement.
NIST SSDF note: Secure settings by default with a documented baseline; no factory-reset requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts mirror (2)(b); the tailor-made carve-out does not remove the reset duty.

NIS2 note: No product updatability requirement; entities patch their own systems.
ISO 27001 note: Patching and change management of own systems; no product update capability or auto-update default.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Update qualification and delivery processes; product update capability sits in IEC 62443-4-2 EDR 3.10.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Support for updates on the component; no automatic-update default, user notification or postponement.
EN 18031 note: Update mechanisms, including automated updates; user notification and postponement are new EN 40000-1-4 controls.
EN 303 645 note: Updatable software, automatic updates and user notification for consumer IoT; JRC-ENISA: no detailed secure update mechanism.
NIST SSDF note: Development practices only; no product updatability requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts add notification and postponement controls missing from EN 18031.

NIS2 note: Access-control and MFA policies for the entity's own systems, not product authentication design.
ISO 27001 clauses: A.5.15; A.5.17; A.5.18; A.8.2; A.8.5 (kit mapping; verify)
ISO 27001 note: Access-control and authentication principles reusable in product design; no product mechanism or unauthorised-access reporting.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Process standard; authentication and access control come from IEC 62443-4-2.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Identification, authentication and authorisation enforcement in depth; JRC-ENISA cites FR1 and CR 2.1. IACS scope.
EN 18031 note: Access control and authentication map closely; unauthorised-access reporting is a new EN 40000-1-4 control (GEC-13).
EN 303 645 note: Authentication and secure communication provisions; no authorisation model or unauthorised-access reporting.
NIST SSDF note: No product authentication or access-control requirements.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts; GEC-13 adds unauthorised-access reporting; EN 304 621 applies access control at every risk tier.

NIS2 note: Entity cryptography policy may inform product choices; no product encryption requirement.
ISO 27001 note: Cryptography and key-management policy feeds the product crypto inventory; product encryption evidence still needed.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Process standard; confidentiality capabilities come from IEC 62443-4-2.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Information confidentiality and cryptography; JRC-ENISA flags key management and deprecated algorithms as gaps.
EN 18031 note: Secure communication, secure storage, keys and best-practice cryptography; RED scope; test evidence reusable.
EN 303 645 note: Secure storage of security parameters, secure communication and personal data; consumer IoT scope.
NIST SSDF note: No product confidentiality or encryption requirements.
CRA drafts* note: Draft vertical clause with a normative cryptography annex; horizontal controls not yet public.

Requirement: Integrity of data, programs and configuration
NIS2 note: No product integrity requirement for data, commands, programs or configuration.
ISO 27001 note: Signatures and change control for organisational assets; no verified boot or product corruption reporting.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: File integrity and private-key controls protect delivered software; product data and configuration integrity sit in 62443-4-2.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Communication, software and session integrity plus boot integrity and roots of trust; enhancements vary by security level.
EN 18031 note: Secure updates and communication integrity; integrity only partly covered and no corruption reporting.
EN 303 645 note: Software integrity and protected security parameters; data and configuration integrity less explicit.
NIST SSDF note: Release integrity verification information; no runtime integrity protection or corruption reporting.
CRA drafts* note: Draft vertical clause mirrors (2)(f); horizontal draft adds an integrity-reporting objective.

NIS2 note: No data-minimisation requirement; GDPR is the relevant reference.
ISO 27001 note: Privacy and PII protection control; product data minimisation needs ISO/IEC 27701-style evidence.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No data-minimisation practice.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No data-minimisation requirement.
EN 18031 note: Protects personal data on radio equipment; minimisation controls (DTM-1..3) are new in EN 40000-1-4.
EN 303 645 note: Personal data protection and data-protection provisions; JRC-ENISA flags deletion and forced-registration gaps.
NIST SSDF note: No data-minimisation requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts; DTM data-minimisation controls are new.

NIS2 note: Business continuity and backup for the entity's services; no product denial-of-service resilience.
ISO 27001 note: Continuity, capacity and redundancy of the entity's services; product-level denial-of-service detail missing.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Defence-in-depth design supports resilience; denial-of-service and recovery capabilities come from 62443-4-2.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Denial-of-service protection, resource management, backup and recovery match availability after an incident. IACS scope.
EN 18031 note: Resilience mechanism carried into EN 40000-1-4; recovery and prioritisation controls RLM-2..6 are new.
EN 303 645 note: Resilience to outages for consumer IoT; product-level denial-of-service detail limited.
NIST SSDF note: No availability or resilience requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts; recovery and prioritisation controls extend EN 18031 RLM-1.

Requirement: Limit impact on other devices and networks
NIS2 note: No duty to limit a product's impact on other networks.
ISO 27001 note: No control on limiting a product's impact on other networks.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No practice on limiting impact on other networks.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Segmentation and zone boundary protection; does not address a product degrading other networks.
EN 18031 note: Traffic control and network monitoring, mainly for network equipment; LIM controls are new in EN 40000-1-4.
EN 303 645 note: JRC-ENISA rates coverage minimal: no network saturation, connection limits or exception handling.
NIST SSDF note: No requirement on impact on other networks.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts close the gap JRC-ENISA rated minimal in existing standards.

NIS2 note: No product attack-surface requirement.
ISO 27001 note: Secure architecture principles only; no product interface inventory or debug-port control.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: General secure design principles; no product interface inventory or debug-lock requirement.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Least functionality and physical diagnostic interface control; JRC-ENISA rates attack-surface coverage principle-level.
EN 18031 note: General equipment capabilities on exposed services and interfaces; RED scope; test evidence reusable.
EN 303 645 note: Minimise exposed attack surfaces; JRC-ENISA judges coverage principle-level rather than concrete controls.
NIST SSDF note: No attack-surface requirement beyond general secure design.
CRA drafts* note: Draft vertical clause mirrors (2)(j); horizontal objectives for (j)-(m) not yet seen.

NIS2 note: No exploitation-mitigation requirement for products.
ISO 27001 note: Secure engineering and coding principles; JRC-ENISA lists 27002 but exploit mitigations are not detailed.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Defence in depth, implementation review and secure coding standards; specific exploit mitigations are not prescribed.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Input validation, deterministic output and restricted data flow; no memory-safety or binary-hardening requirement.
EN 18031 note: General capabilities only; no exploit mitigations such as ASLR, W^X or sandboxing.
EN 303 645 note: Listed by JRC-ENISA; defence in depth and sandboxing not detailed; no binary-hardening provisions.
NIST SSDF note: Secure coding and hardened compiler and build settings; sandboxing and privilege separation not prescribed.
CRA drafts* note: Draft vertical clause; draft EN 304 626 adds detailed memory-safety and hardening families for operating systems.

NIS2 note: No product logging capability or user opt-out.
ISO 27001 note: Logging and monitoring requirements inform the product event catalogue; no product-level logging or user opt-out.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Process standard; logging capabilities come from IEC 62443-4-2.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Auditable events, audit storage, timestamps, non-repudiation and monitoring; no user opt-out.
EN 18031 note: NMM-1 network monitoring (EN 18031-1) and the LGM logging mechanism (EN 18031-2/-3, privacy and financial assets) within RED scope; no user opt-out.
EN 303 645 note: Telemetry examination only; JRC-ENISA finds no explicit protected security-event logging.
NIST SSDF note: No product logging requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Draft treats logging as essential in every use case; opt-out for components without a user interface unresolved.

NIS2 note: No product data-removal or transfer requirement.
ISO 27001 note: Information deletion on organisational storage; no user-facing secure erase or data transfer.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Secure disposal guidelines document data removal; product erase capability and data transfer not required.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Information persistence (purging); no ease-of-use requirement for users and no secure data transfer.
EN 18031 note: Deletion mechanism in the privacy-oriented parts; no secure transfer. EN 40000-1-4 adds SO.FactoryReset.
EN 303 645 note: Easy deletion of user data; lacks detailed deletion guidance and secure data transfer.
NIST SSDF note: No data-removal requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Drafts; EN 304 621 does not require transfer, which the CRA requires where data can be transferred.

NIS2 note: No SBOM duty; NIS2 customers may demand one under Art 21(2)(d) supply-chain measures.
ISO 27001 note: Asset inventory and ICT supply-chain controls; no SBOM or machine-readable component list.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Requirements for externally provided components and dependent-component update documentation; no SBOM.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Component inventory capability of the control system; not an SBOM.
EN 18031 note: Showing no known vulnerabilities implies a component inventory; no SBOM requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No SBOM requirement.
NIST SSDF note: Provenance data for all release components, with SBOM as an example; no minimum content or format.
CRA drafts* note: Requires an SBOM per product (§5.2); draft at formal vote, citation 2027 at the earliest.

NIS2 note: Vulnerability handling for the entity's own systems; no duty to remediate shipped products.
ISO 27001 note: Triage and remediation process transfers; JRC-ENISA lists 27001/27002; no separation of security and feature updates.
IEC 62443-4-1 clauses: DM-1; DM-2; DM-3; DM-4 (kit mapping; verify)
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Defect management covers triage and remediation; JRC-ENISA lists 4-1; separation of security and feature updates not addressed.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Product capabilities only; remediation process sits in IEC 62443-4-1 DM.
EN 18031 note: Updatable and free of known vulnerabilities at placing; no ongoing remediation process.
EN 303 645 note: Act on reported vulnerabilities and provide timely security updates; no separation of security and feature updates.
NIST SSDF note: Assess, prioritise and remediate, plus root-cause analysis; no separation of security and feature updates.
CRA drafts* note: Covers all eight Part II points, including update separation; clause-level text for point 2 not reviewed.

NIS2 note: Assessing effectiveness of entity measures; not product security testing.
ISO 27001 note: Security testing in development and acceptance; no cadence or method guidance, so add threat-driven re-test triggers.
IEC 62443-4-1 clauses: SVV-1; SVV-2; SVV-3; SVV-4 (kit mapping; verify)
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Per-release security testing; CRA adds threat-driven review and re-testing through the support period.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No testing cadence; product test evidence feeds point 3 only indirectly.
EN 18031 note: Assessment at placing only; no regular testing through the support period.
EN 303 645 note: No regular security testing requirement.
NIST SSDF note: Code review, executable testing and ongoing vulnerability identification; cadence left to the organisation.
CRA drafts* note: Planned tests and regular testing during support, a gap earlier drafts left; draft, not cited.

NIS2 note: Vulnerability disclosure named at entity level; no advisory content or timing for products.
ISO 27001 note: No duty to publish advisories on fixed product vulnerabilities.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Disclosing security-related issues; JRC-ENISA notes no disclosure timelines or standard format.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No disclosure requirement.
EN 18031 note: No disclosure requirement.
EN 303 645 note: Listed by JRC-ENISA; no advisory content, format or timing for fixed vulnerabilities.
NIST SSDF note: Advisories appear only as example implementations; no public disclosure duty or required content.
CRA drafts* note: Machine-readable advisories (RLS-2, §10.2); draft built on ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111; required content and delay rules not confirmed at clause level; not cited.

NIS2 note: Designates CSIRTs as CVD coordinators, the anonymous route a CRA CVD policy should offer; no manufacturer policy duty.
ISO 27001 note: Vulnerability management guidance only; no requirement to publish and enforce a CVD policy.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Intake and disclosure processes exist; no requirement to publish a CVD policy or offer anonymous reporting.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No CVD policy requirement.
EN 18031 note: No CVD policy requirement.
EN 303 645 note: Publish a vulnerability disclosure policy; JRC-ENISA notes enforcement of the policy is not addressed.
NIST SSDF note: Expects a vulnerability disclosure policy and supporting process; publication and anonymous route not specified.
CRA drafts* note: CVD policy with a 7-day acknowledgement cap, as reported by ENISA; draft, not cited.

NIS2 note: No product contact-address or third-party information-sharing duty.
ISO 27001 note: Contacts with authorities and special-interest groups; no public vulnerability contact or third-party sharing duty.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Receiving reports from external sources; third-party component information sharing not covered.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No contact-address or information-sharing requirement.
EN 18031 note: No contact-address or information-sharing requirement.
EN 303 645 note: Public contact point for reporting; third-party component information sharing not covered.
NIST SSDF note: Gathering vulnerability information, including on third-party components; no public contact-address requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Secure reporting channel; third-party component sharing detail not confirmed in reviewed summaries.

NIS2 note: No secure update distribution requirement for products.
ISO 27001 note: Controlled installation on operational systems; JRC-ENISA lists 27002 but finds no explicit requirement to publish hashes, verification instructions or code-signing certificates.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Update delivery and signing-key protection; JRC-ENISA: no explicit hashes, verification or code-signing certificates.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Update support and software integrity verification on the component; distribution infrastructure and auto-update not covered.
EN 18031 note: Secure and automated update mechanisms on the device; distribution infrastructure and signing-key management not covered.
EN 303 645 note: Secure update provisions for consumer IoT; JRC-ENISA, mapping 5.3 to Part I (2)(c), finds no detailed secure update mechanism; not listed for point 7.
NIST SSDF note: Protects code and publishes release integrity information; automatic distribution and anti-rollback not covered.
CRA drafts* note: Secure update distribution provision; clause content beyond its label not reviewed.

NIS2 note: No duty to disseminate free security updates.
ISO 27001 note: JRC-ENISA cites legacy control 12.6 (now 8.8); no free-of-charge updates or advisory messages.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Timely patch delivery with disclosure; JRC-ENISA: free-of-charge updates and notification methods not explicit.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No dissemination or free-of-charge requirement.
EN 18031 note: No dissemination or free-of-charge requirement.
EN 303 645 note: Timely updates with user notification; free-of-charge dissemination not addressed.
NIST SSDF note: No dissemination or free-of-charge requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Expected to cover dissemination; free-of-charge and advisory detail not confirmed at clause level.

NIS2 note: Entity risk-analysis method reusable; CRA assessment must cover each Annex I item per product.
ISO 27001 note: ISMS risk assessment and treatment reusable; BSI TR-03183-H adds CRA refinements; per-item product justification needed.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Threat model and security context reusable; CRA needs per-item Annex I applicability with justifications.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Target security levels presuppose a risk assessment (IEC 62443-3-2); per-item CRA justification still needed.
EN 18031 note: Decision-tree rationale documents applicability per mechanism; CRA needs a product risk assessment with per-item justification.
EN 303 645 note: Justifies non-applied provisions; not a product risk assessment covering each Annex I item.
NIST SSDF note: Risk modelling informs design; CRA needs documented per-item Annex I applicability and justifications.
CRA drafts* note: Covers risk assessment and lifecycle under Art 13(2)-(3); no citation expected, so evidence only.

NIS2 note: Supplier-assessment process and records transfer; open-source component analysis and EUVD checks need adding.
ISO 27001 clauses: A.5.19; A.5.20; A.5.21; A.5.22 (kit mapping; verify)
ISO 27001 note: Supplier controls transfer; guidance para 207 accepts 27001 for remote services; open-source component checks need adding.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Security requirements for externally provided and supplier-developed components; add EUVD checks and open-source records.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No component due-diligence requirement.
EN 18031 note: No component due-diligence requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No component due-diligence requirement.
NIST SSDF note: Third-party requirements and verification of acquired components; add EUVD checks and support-period review.
CRA drafts* note: No draft clause on component due diligence identified; use the CRA text, FAQ and guidance.

NIS2 note: No duty to report vulnerabilities to upstream component maintainers.
ISO 27001 note: No duty to report vulnerabilities to upstream component maintainers.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No duty to report component vulnerabilities to upstream maintainers.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No upstream-reporting requirement.
EN 18031 note: No upstream-reporting requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No upstream-reporting requirement.
NIST SSDF note: No upstream-reporting requirement.
CRA drafts* note: No draft clause on upstream reporting identified; follow guidance paras 222-229.

NIS2 note: No support-period duty; NIS2 customers may request it contractually.
ISO 27001 note: No support-period determination.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No support-period determination practice.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No support-period requirement.
EN 18031 note: No support-period requirement.
EN 303 645 note: Publish the defined support period; the CRA also requires determining it, normally at least five years.
NIST SSDF note: No support-period requirement.
CRA drafts* note: No standard covers support-period determination; use Art 13(8) and guidance paras 125-128.

NIS2 note: No product technical documentation requirement.
ISO 27001 note: Documented-information discipline helps; Annex VII content is CRA-specific and not covered.
IEC 62443-4-1 clauses: SR-2; SVV-1; SG-1; SG-7 (kit mapping; verify)
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Threat model, test records and user guidelines feed Annex VII points 2, 3 and 6; no dossier structure.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Capability evidence and test reports feed Annex VII points 5 and 6; no dossier requirement.
EN 18031 note: Rationale and test evidence feed Annex VII points 5 and 6; RED evidence shows RED, not CRA, conformity.
EN 303 645 note: Conformance statement and TS 103 701 test reports feed Annex VII points 5 and 6; no dossier requirement.
NIST SSDF note: Provenance and test records feed Annex VII points 2(b) and 6; no dossier requirement.
CRA drafts* note: Clause-to-Annex I mapping table helps structure Annex VII point 5; dossier content comes from the Regulation.

NIS2 note: Covers significant incidents, not vulnerabilities; reuse the 24h/72h runbook and awareness test. Filed separately.
ISO 27001 clauses: A.5.5; A.5.24; A.5.25; A.5.26 (kit mapping; verify)
ISO 27001 note: Incident management and authority contacts reusable; no exploited-vulnerability trigger, 24h/72h/14-day clock or SRP filing.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No reporting-to-authorities duty; defect triage can feed the exploitation decision.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No reporting requirement.
EN 18031 note: No reporting requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No reporting requirement.
NIST SSDF note: No reporting requirement.
CRA drafts* note: No standard covers SRP reporting; Art 14 and the ENISA SRP glossary govern.

NIS2 note: Same 24h/72h/1-month structure and awareness test; the proposed Art 23(12) deeming rule is not adopted, so file separately.
ISO 27001 note: Incident assessment and response process reusable; no CRA severe-incident test, timelines or SRP filing.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: No reporting-to-authorities duty or severe-incident test.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No reporting requirement.
EN 18031 note: No reporting requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No reporting requirement.
NIST SSDF note: No reporting requirement.
CRA drafts* note: No standard covers SRP reporting; Art 14 and the ENISA SRP glossary govern.

NIS2 note: Informing service recipients of incidents and remedies parallels CRA user information; trigger and audience differ.
ISO 27001 note: Incident response includes communication; no duty to inform product users or machine-readable notices.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Disclosure to product users exists; no awareness-triggered notice or machine-readable format.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: No user-notification requirement.
EN 18031 note: No user-notification requirement.
EN 303 645 note: No awareness-triggered user notification requirement.
NIST SSDF note: No user-notification requirement.
CRA drafts* note: No draft clause on Art 14(8) user information identified; follow guidance paras 219-221.

NIS2 note: No conformity assessment of products.
ISO 27001 note: BSI TR-03183-H extends a 27001 ISMS to carry Module H; certification alone gives no conformity.
IEC 62443-4-1 note: Not expected to be cited for the CRA; certification gives no presumption of conformity.
IEC 62443-4-2 note: Not expected to be cited; prEN 50770 OT profiles will be the CRA vehicle.
EN 18031 note: Cited only under RED; RED certificates valid to 11 Jun 2028 evidence RED, not CRA, conformity.
EN 303 645 note: Not cited under the CRA; no presumption of conformity.
NIST SSDF note: Not EU-recognised; no presumption or conformity route.
